To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
A numerical implementation of the dynamic thermal network method is presented and the accuracy of the method is shown to be comparable with numerical methods.
a novel numerical approach to the calculation of weighting factors for the Dynamic Thermal Network approach to the modelling transient conduction in multi dimensional bodies has been developed.

a numerical implementation of the DTN method for long time scale simulation of conduction problems is presented; the numerical procedure allows the generation of DTN weighting factor data in an automated fashion; and the numerical procedure has been shown to be accurate and efficient.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a new numerical approach to the calculation of the weighting factor data necessary to implement the Dynamic Thermal Network approach to modelling transient conduction in non-homogeneous multi-dimensional solids.

the development and validation of a numerical implementation of the DTN method and the application of this to the long timescales simulation of conduction heat transfer in multi-dimensional nonhomogeneous solids.
the development of a numerical method to generate the necessary data to implement the DTN method in a long timescale simulation environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DTN method is a useful addition to the armoury of the building energy analyst.
the DTN method is an efficient numerical method for long timescale conduction problems in multi-dimensional geometries.
the DTN approach is an efficient and accurate method for simulating transient conduction in complex multi-dimensional geometries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method can be used to simulate long time series conduction in complex multi-dimensional geometries in a very efficient way.

the DTN method can be applied to the simulation of long timescale transient conduction in multi-dimension, complex geometries with a high degree of accuracy and at a computational cost that is comparable to the use of a numerical method.
the DTN approach is a promising method for long time scale simulation of building components, especially for the modelling of the thermal performance of massive structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DTN method is well suited for the simulation of long-term transient conduction problems in complex geometries.

the DTN approach can be used to simulate long timescale transient heat conduction in multi-dimensionally complex bodies with a high level of accuracy and at a computational cost that is orders of magnitude less than other numerical methods.
the DTN approach is a viable alternative to numerical methods for long timescale simulation, particularly for the simulation of building components.
